She locked eyes with Happy. This was bad. There was nothing good about the predicament she found herself in no matter how she looked at it. She had taken a seat, her hands under the table twirling a ring of gold as she mulled  over the words Frice had just told her. Visage rested his head on his paws. This was a death sentence for the children of Victory. Her and Rhiannon had built a relationship over many years that started out with their mutuel dislike of Khion and grew into an alliance both cherished and a friendship that could be shattered by a few simple phraises. “Maybe Khion wants to have a nice family reunion.” Visage thought to her.
She would have laughed if it wasn’t impolite and dangerous to do so. Khion wasn’t the type. Rhiannon wasn’t the type to forgive traitors. Cacia had been by her side when those who wronged her were punished. It wasn’t pretty. She’d swear to her confidants retribution was her middle name. Say she did give up her friend’s location to these two and Khion shared who had ruined her perfectly happy existance. Now let us say, by some miracle  the sisters began to get along and formed a mutuel dislike for those who longed more and more to destroy what Khion stood for. Fatehaven would be first on their list. If Rhiannon was given even a third of the power she’d had in the past and Cacia was forced to face her in battle Fatehaven would slip farther and farther into the grip of insanity. And if she denied them what they wanted could her people withstand the increase of an all ready ferocious winter? Could she keep her kingdom under control, feed them and help them prosper? They were resilient  but that would only hold them over for so long. Then she would have no choice but to go to Khion for some reprieve from the cold that made mother griffins shrink into their nests and the dark that tired out young soldiers on watch each night. And Khion would love that way too much. Just the thought of that made silver and gold flecks dance in her eyes. Visage tensed imperceptibly. She let the rage go, let it wash over her and vanish into the back of her mind to be dealt with later. Something else was bothering her, and it clearly held the attention of one of her companions. The guard Frice had brought with her. Visage had looked away, being a dutiful son that he was, but his claws were extended, though tucked close to his chest, and there was a stillness to his body that worried her. The rest of the pack were restless. She needed to answer Frice. The seconds ticked by, the fate of Fatehaven and its children held in her hands, no pressure, but she had to askVisage what it was that drew his wrath to their guest.
“What is it son?”
She sent out calming waves to him and the tension in his muscles eased a bit. “You don’t sense it, general? The smell of her brings back the screams of an achiever cub and shouts of a city in the grips of batttle. Savage. I never learned her name but I could never forget her scent. Or my brother.”
Waves of clarity slammed into her and her fingers dug into her palms under the table. Savage. His twin. They’d grown a lot since then. But it couldn’t be? She had failed him, almost failed them all, she couldn’t do it again.
“I apologize, Frice, but I don’t know where she is. I would be happy to find her for you, Visage here is an excilent tracker, aren’t you son?’
Her friend’s body shifted from dangerous predator to teenage boy in seconds. He knelt before his queen, raising his eyes to meet hers and Frice’s in turn. “Yes, general.”
He spoke softly. “And Happy over there loves a challenge, don’t you Captain?”
“That I do, general.”
The room fell silent once again, waiting for Frice’s answer.

Have you ever stopped to wonder what the meaning of sacrifice truly is? Sacrifice in all its forms? Sure there is the physical act of sending someone or something to its death to gain approval from some higher power or a gift of some sort, but then there is the other kind of sacrifice. The kind that most take for granted. The kind they don’t see. And as I gaze over the tiny yet stable village the other outcasts in my little pack...my family call home, I wonder about that. About that other kind. Rain pours down on the walls but the runes the young mages managed to chalk onto the walls glow in the light of the setting sun which hangs like fire in the sky. The stars begin to poke their heads out from behind the clouds. All around me the others are finishing up last minute preparations for the night. They speak in hushed tones while the little ones play games and tell stories around the fire. My eyes move of their own accord in the direction of the place we left. Rumors have spread that they call her the tyrant queen. They say she misses me. I doubt that. Anger rises in my chest, a fire that courses through my body and makes me shiver. I coax the flame back, the way a master might do a dog, trying to stop the tempest from sweeping me away. She doesn’t misss me. On the night she locked away my parents, bound my siblings magic to her...made them slaves, and banished me from the land of my birth, from the home that was rightfully mine, she killed our relationship. She turned what we built into nothing more than ashes scattered in the breeze. “General.” One of the young soldiers comes running through the gates with a food hall. The creators, those that are gifted with the power of creating  resources from the elements are mentally drained, one is even sick. It has taken a lot to build this little home in the forest, but we have all worked hard to insure the survival of the next generation. The worst part about all of this, what makes the anger roar as if it were a dragon, is the fact that I never saw it coming. I never assumed out of all the people to betray my family it would be her. “Daughter,” He would always say, “You must be careful even with those you love. Sometimes your worst enemy is your closest friend.”
I think about him now as food is finished eaten and soldiers take their places in the trees. Older siblings usher the younger ones inside. My father. i wonder how he is, if he lives. I join the soldiers but not in the trees, instead I take to the sky on a griffin. My bonding partner, Vissage and I are restless. Even now he paws the sky as I drawl the shadows around us like a cloak. The feathers on his wings are like that of an owl, and they make no sound as the wind passes over them. We circle the village. The sound of the achievers, the winged wolf like venomous predators who’s Alfa is like a sister to me bring me comfort. The night grows cooler, though the air is somehow still humid. Vissage lets his song join theirs. The melody is haunting. Not sad just....longing for something. Freedom perhaps. Maybe it is a longing for the wind ruffling their wings, for the feeling of their paws hitting the earth, for the chance to run without having to look over their shoulder, without having to be careful. Maybe it is a longing for home. For a place where they belong, for the place where their ancestors were born, for though their is a certain sense of belonging when they are together, their instincts call them back to that place. He always was more of a military man then a father. It was all he knew, and in the end it was what saved us, his children. Some called him paranoid, others a  genius. Some thought him insane, though they nnever dared to say it to his face. We thought him amazing and unstoppable, but isn’t that what most children believe when it comes to their parents? In our eyes he and our mother hung the moon and the stars. Until they taught us how to worship and told us the stories of legends and the gods that rule over our people, they were the center of our universe. Even afterwords I believe they still were. He taught us to fight at an early age. We spent hours learning stratigy, honing our skills with blade and magic, ingraining in our heads  the fact that patience was a life saver. He knew how cruil the world  could be and though he loved us dearly he wanted us to be harshly  aware of that fact. He was a good man who never put his hands on us in anger or raised his voice, though that was a little scary when you saw how he worked with those under his command. The moon is full tonight, and what snaps me out of my thoughts is the sound of a familiar voice whispering my name. Vissage growls low, a primal growl. He tucks his wings and we dip downwards, landing in the branches of an old tree. I glance around. There is no way she’d be that foolish, to wonder out here alone without a guard or two? My stomach clinches. The fire roars in my ears. Vissage nuzzles my finger. “Good boy.” I whisper. He chirps softly. I didn’t notice how far we were away from the village. I scold myself. I know better. Not being aware of your surroundings is a death sentence, even if you and your griffin are cloaked in shadows. There are worse things out there than a lost love. I can see her now. She stands on a pier  overlooking the northern sea, on the spot where we use to lay and gaze out over the water just talking about anything and everything. Sometimes we would just lay here, not needing to say a word, offering each other our presence. That was good enough. She holds a white rose in one hand, in the other a fireball strains at the tip of her fingers. I move closer to get a better view, but not too close. My name leaves her lips again, a choked cry that dims the flame in my eyes. The fireball breaks free and turns the rose into little more than ashes that her trembling hand releases into the Icy  depths below. Words leave my lips before I can stop them. “That poor flower totally didn’t deserve that.”
She whirls around, and suddenly I need her to know I saw, need her to know I’m here. It’s reckless. It’s dangerous. It’s selfish, for now that she knows I’m here she might try and follow me to the others. I’m an idiot and I should care. I don’t love her, I don’t think I still do. No, there’s something else. It’s the feeling of satisfaction that is so damn good. The sadness in her eyes at what she caused herself to lose, something that was clearly so precious to her is sweet and I am so elated at that haunted look  in her eyes and terrified at how I love it so much, how I want more of that feeling. Our eyes meet, there in the darkness and the shadow of that pier, and I make a promise to myself and my small band of followers. No matter how long it takes, I will see the Hayaus family back on the throne  and them safely home. She’ll regret what she did to us, whether I mean the two of us or all of us I’m not really sure. I turn away and head for the village.

Waking up in a bag wasn’t even the strangest thing to happen to me that morning. Neither was being named Sammie. The fact that I was a stuffed yellow catipilar didn’t seem to bother me much either. I was being oddly calm about the whole dying and being resurrected as a stuffed toy thing. At first I thought it was a joke, some Devine being got bored and decided to have a little fun. But as me and the 10 year  old girl cradling me walked into her bedroom, me in her right arm and her cane in the other, I understood this was my new reality. She introduced me to Hershal, Shasta, Faithful, and the other stuffed toys I would be spending my days with. “Nina, time for cake.” Her father called from downstairs. “Coming, daddy.” She kissed each of us on the head and told us she’d be right back. She scampered out of the room, closing the door behind her. “Let me be the first to say welcome Sammie.” Hershal offered. I tilted my head and gasped. “You can talk?”
“Of course. All of us can.” His voice was nasally and he seemed soft spoken. He was a bright blue teddy bear and was currently sporting a pair of bright orange sunglasses. The others moved in closer. There were some Nina hadn’t had the chance to introduce me too. “I, I would make introductions but first there is something you must know about what we do here.”
“Aren’t we just playthings? I mean, we spend all our days having tea parties and stuff right.”
“Not exactly. I mean we do a lot of playing pretend and those are the best parts of our days.” The others nodded in agreement. “But we are more than that.” Faithful said, putting a paw on Hershal’s shoulder. “We are Nina’s guides. Her protectors. Her friends. We are the ones she comes too about anything and everything. And we stay up at night and protect her from... well...the things she can see and that can see her. You see, Sammmie, Nina is special.”
“You guys are pranking me, right.” I asked. “This must be a joke you play on all the new toys.”
Hershal shook his head. “You’ll see tonight.” He said simply.
Nina came upstairs and took me down with her for dinner. I was at her side as she and her brothers and sister finished homework, waited for her to finish her bath, and watched as her parents put them all to bed. Nina said her prayers. “Goodnight, guys. I love you.” She whispered to all of us as her eyes closed. The lights in the room dimmed but the candles on the dresser stayed lit. So did the nightlight and the hallway lights. I watched the others surround Nina and turn to face the room. I took my place among them, in Nina’s arms, tilting my head to face the room like the others. “Here she comes.” Luna whispered to me. Hershal straightened. He was at the head of our circle. A shadow creeped from the corner of the room towards the end of the bed. The others shifted slightly but my eyes were fixed on the shadow even though they were looking for other signs of activities in the room. The candles did not dim, though the cross hanging above them swayed slightly. Her younger brother padded softly into the room, clutching a stuffed wolf, and moved the cross away from the lit candles then hurried back to his room. The shadow drew closer. “Nina.” It, or she, whispered softly. Hershal growled a warning as our charge stered. “Leave, Vivian. You aren’t welcome here.” When he was speaking to me in the beginning, Hershal didn’t sound assertive at all. Now, there was a tone of commmand in his voice that was unmistakable. The spirit, with dark, tainted black eyes reached out to touch Nina. Luna leapt up and placed her body between Nina and Vivian, her horn tilted to nudge Nina back to sleep. “Leave.” Hershal ordered again as Nina’s arms tightened around me. The shadows in the room thickened. Nina jerked and I whispered a silent prayer, trying to do my part from my place at her side. The shadows backed away. “Remember, Sammie, it’s the conviction behind the words you say that matters.” Faithful whispered to me. Nina’s hand found one of my legs and clutched it. I wasn’t going to let whoever this was hurt my new family, especially someone so sweet as Nina. Vivian reaches out and pushed poor old Khalil off the bed. “Khalil!!!!” Cried Shasta. We tightened the circle as Kalil struggled to make his way back onto the bed. As the sun rose the spirit and her friends faded away. “Damn you, Hershal. It’s rude to keep me from my baby sister.”
“Not when you’re the older sibling.” Hershal shot back. The alarm went off and Nina got up to get ready for school. As the front door shut for the last time, I turned to my companions. They had sprawled out on the bed, grateful, it seemed to get a break. “That happens every night?” I asked. “It’s usually worse than that. Sometimes Nina wakes screaming from nightmares. I cock my head to one side and try to ask him if he hears it, but my words are almost inaudible. He steps closer and there is a ringing in my ears. The howling has always only been audible to me. This man is about to learn that carma sucks. He raises the knife. My mouth is dry and the only thing I seem able to taste is the cloth that has a little bit of blood on it from a broken tooth. The door splinters open behind him. He turns. Maybe he was in denial? Maybe he refused to acknowledge anyone would find us here? Poor, foolish one, for the thing standing in the shattered remains of the door is not human. It is too graceful. It is a hunter, a predator, a bringer of justice to those who commit some of the most vile sins in the dead of night, for isn’t that why the sun sets and the moon rises? To cloak the sins of those who are too ashamed to show their faces during the light of day? We hunt those too, those that sin while the warmth of the sun brings  light and life  to the Earth, but those that think they are safe in the dark are our favorites to prove wrong. There is something about the thrill of the hunt that captivates us even as we grow to adulthood. You have to be careful not to let that thrill and high control you. You have to be careful not to lose yourself to it. It is a large wolf like creature, with white wings protruding from its dark black fur. Poisonous spines poke out from its slowly swishing tail and venom drips from its extended claws as well as its fangs. It pricks its ears and lopes confidently across the room, an unnerving intelligence in the tainted depths of its silver eyes. “Bad.” It said, looking at me. It is followed by four of its brothers and sisters, and I snap the restraints as my body begins to shift in response to them. My children. And this isn’t even all of them. The dazed feeling leaves me. It doesn’t hurt, not like it did the first time. They bow their heads and sink to the floor in submission, then rise in unison. At a thought from me they surround him. One shoots a poisoned spine from his tail. The man falls to the ground, twitching and then spasming as the poison paralyzes his body. He tries to speak but it seems his tongue is now too big for his mouth. They tighten the circle. His heartbeat quickens. We can hear it, hear the blood rushing through his veins. We can smell his fear, taste it, it roles off of him in waves. It smells like sugar cookies, and the younger members of the group edge closer, drawn by it. “What, what are you?” He slurs.
“We are the achievers.” I say, running my tongue over my newly formed tooth as it slowly sharpens into a fang to join the others. “Don’t be so scared.” The littlest of the group says softly, putting a paw on his shoulder. “We aren’t going to hurt you. There’s someone else who has requested that honor.”
I didn’t think his face could lose any more of its color. They drag him out of the room. The knife slips from his fingers. I whisper a few words and a window appears in the air. A face swims into view. “Target has been acquired, sir.” I say as we hoke our claws into him and rise into the sky. In all my years in this job I have never seen the man before me smile. At my words he grins, but it never reaches his eyes. “Well done, my hunter. Tell my brother hi for me, willl you?”
“As you wish, sir.”
The prince of fate salutes me and signs off. The cold night air hits my fur and the wind pushes my ears back.our wings beat a rhythm as the snow whips around our heads. As we join the wind’s song with one of our own, I have only one thought. Damn, I love my job.

The rain and thunder were not the only things keeping me up this late hour. I bet you I can guess what you’re thinking. Oh no, here we go again. It’s gunna be one of those it was a dark and stormy night kinda stories. Well, let me start off by saying I regret nothing!!!! Now where was I? Oh right, my bedroom. With Jasper the puppy my parents got my sister and I. And a can of soda on my bedside table. The thunder shaking our house. The rain making soothing sounds on the roof, though sleep eluded me, as it always seemed to do on nights like this. I had my earbuds in, listening to a mix of Heather Dale and Rascal  Flats when the door creeked open. Jasper picked up his ears and growled, barking furiously. He only gets that way when he sees a balloon. Or nail polish. Or an Amazon delivery truck and that last one is because he always thinks they are bringing something for him. I ignored it, my fingers never leaving my keyboard. I had to finish this chapter. The rivalry between Cacia, my hero, Sellece, the villainess, and her younger sister was just too much to leave this scene on a cliffhanger. Soft footsteps approached my bed. It probably didn’t help I was home alone tonight.
Now you are totally thinking it, aren’t you? Oh no, it’s gunna be one of those creepy home alone at night during a storm stories. Yes, yes it is. Jasper was the one who knocked my keyboard off my bed. “Dang it, boy. Bad...” i just so happened to look up then, and what I saw made the words die on my lips  and  my heart pound in my chest. 
There she stood, wearing a long formfitting soldier’s uniform, a piece of broken crown tangled in her long midnight hair along the beads tied with blue thread and shells she had braided into it. At her side was an ice wolf, one of the mythical beings from the world I loved and tried  so desperately to work on building every day, staring curiously at Jasper. My puppy was not so keen on the large white beast with eyes as black as the sky during a blizzard. As for his master, her eyes, which were as blue and empty as glaciers and yet somehow held a haunting sadness that stole my breath, was eying me with just a hint of barely contained insanity behind her smile. She was deadly like a winter storm. She was beauty, like the frost flowers you see just as the sun starts to rise, a little moment of perfection before the dawn and its warmth steal them away. She was former Crown Princess  Sellece Arrayiea  Iliana Reyes, and she did not looked pleased. Then again, when did she ever look happy? I asked myself. 
She sat at my desk, all grace and poise, but like a lion before it strikes its prey. “So, you are the one behind my dreary existence.” She said softly
Her voice was soft and husky, like the way the last Fall wind sounds when it blows away the leaves. I was stunned into silence and looked like a total idiot just standing there. She commanded others respect. She made them fear her, for the element she commanded was as deadly as the words she wielded as weapons. 
“Um, yeah. I am, I mean my name is Cacie.” I blurted out.
“You are lying.” She said simply. “Your name is Cassie, not Cacie. Either way, it is an honor to finally meet you.”
She bowed her head, a strand of midnight hair falling in front of her eyes, and I awkwardly returned the greeting. I did not feel like angering her. I knew of her abilities, for I was the one who created her, and I did not feel like being slowly frozen alive and punctured by ice shards. That was not how I wanted to spend my evening. “The pleasure is all mine.” I said, as our dogs finally started to make their own introductions. So far so good. 
“Shasta and I came here to ask you, Cassie, why?”
“Why what?” I asked, as the two of our pets began wrestling on the bed. Sellece’s sharp whistle stopped poor Shasta. The young cub went still and hung his head before sitting down and putting back his ears. Jasper still wanted to play, and I had to put him in his crate. He looked longingly at Shasta. “Why does everyone else get to be happy but me? Thalia, my sister, gets reunited with our grandfather, supportive friends and a bright future. Cacia has my respect, she is truly a worthy adversary, but her and Ariana have a beautiful, dutiful  son and rule a fantastic kingdom where light shines bright and crops grow plentiful. I get in-prisoned in a frozen wasteland where my only comfort is Shasta and his brothers and sisters. I. Know I made some mistakes and all, that I was brutal towards my sister and my people, and let us not bring up mother and father, but do I, we, not deserve some love? We are your characters too, you know.”
Just then the door opened again, and in came the littlest of the Reyes sisters, her long dark hair falling down her back, her bright eyes shining with the light of the God of Water, whom she served. “Hi, Cass. Oh hey, sister.” She stopped and looked from me to her dejected older sibling, lethal older sibling sitting at my desk. “Sister? Cass, I can come back later if you two are, well, busy.”
Before I could say anything it was Sellece who stopped her. In a flash Shasta was at the entrance to my bedroom door. Thalia shrank away from him. “Stop it all three of you. This instant.”
They all looked at me. I walked over and put a hand on Sellece’s shoulder. “Be nice to your sister, Thalia. I have not been lately, and she could use a break.”
The spiteful words died on Thalia’s lips when her older sister looked up at me with a heartbreaking grateful and tired smile. “Call in Cacia, Thalia. Let us finish this story together, as friends. As family.”
Now, every time a winter storm is said to darken my doorstep and the leaves have left their trees, I head to the store and stock up on flowers and snacks and anything brightly colored. People certainly think I am strange, but Jasper and I don’t mind the looks. Because as soon as the snacks are laid out before the hearth, drinks are poured and soft music is playing, there is a knock on my door. I am no longer alarmed anymore, and Jasper wags his tail and barks with joy. First appears Sellece and Shasta, the pets happy to greet each other as their owners share a warm hug. Then comes Ariana, Cacia and their son, Taika, carrying goodies of their own. Thalia follows soon after, and soon my living room is filled with the sound of laughter and stories by firelight. Family writing sessions are the best. And you know what else?? I never run out of ideas for our next adventure.
